LESSON: VISUAL PROGRAMMING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication
Topic 2.4: Visual Programming
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Visual Programming, part of Communication in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are computer programs used in daily life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Visual Programming together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Learner develops speaking, listening and team working skills when discussing the

features of a visual programming application

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Learner develops open mindedness and creativity skills when applying effects

such as sound, animations, background in a program

Value:

Responsibility: Learner engages in assigned roles and duties when using visual programming software to create instructions in

the work environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer Education: Learner enhances healthy inter and intra personal relationships with others when searching for information on

terminologies used in visual programming and discussing with peers.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate the skills used in visual programming to solving problems in Mathematics

Suggested Learning Resources

Digital devices, Apps, productivity tools, visual programming tools, adapted computer software (OS, Utility software and

Application programs) Internet, adapted drawing tables

Other related services: Physiotherapy, Occupation Therapy, Speech Therapy, Learners Support Assistant
